newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool prices seen rising in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool prices seen rising in 2nd half.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to be higher in the second half of the current season because of a gradual strengthening of demand in Western Europe and steady demand in China, Wool International (WI) said.

WI said in its latest Insight publication that the eastern market indicator was expected to average 620 cents a kg clean in the second half of the season after averaging 580 cents a kg in the first half.
This would result in an average of 600 cents a kg clean for the 1996/97 season ending June 30, it said.
The indicator fell by 29 cents to 568 cents a kg clean at the close of trading in December 1996 from the end of the last season, WI said.
At sales this week, the first of the second half of the season, the eastern indicator rose about three percent or by 16 cents to 584 cents a kg clean.
The indicator was 12 percent lower in the first six months of the current season than in the same period last season, WI said.
WI said an estimated 520 million kg of wool remained available for sale in the second half of the 1996/97 season from total forecast availability for the full season of 905 million kg.
WI said it assumed it would sell 135,000 bales of stockpile wool in both the March and June quarters.

At December 31, its forward sold position for the March 1997 quarter was 64,384 bales, or 48 percent of the new legislated minimum sales requirement. A further 1,453 bales had been sold into the June 1997 quarter, it said.
WI sales in the December 1996 quarter were 184,611 bales.
Little improvement had occurred in the economic situation or outlook over the past month in the major wool consuming countries, it said.
